about: ASEAN Watch fire snapshot written by scripts/refresh-fires.mjs from the four NASA FIRMS 7-day South East Asia CSVs. MEASURED satellite detections only (VIIRS confidence nominal or high, MODIS confidence 50 or more). Fire radiative power (FRP, MW) is a proxy for fire intensity, not emissions; CAMS GFAS (Fire Emissions Watch) converts FRP to emissions. No detections in a cell does not mean no fire: cloud, smoke and overpass timing hide fires.

periods.note: Index 0 is the 24 h before the reference time, index 6 the 24 h ending 144 h before it.

coverageNote: The files cover from 00:00 UTC of the first date present in all four. A period that starts earlier can miss the tail of one night pass; the first date is also left out of the complete-day history in case it is partial.

filters.note: Same thresholds as the watch rules in src/lib/watchRules.ts. Low-confidence detections are counted per source but not used.

method.countries: Point in polygon against data/region.geojson (Natural Earth); points up to 0.15° outside a coastline go to that country; the rest are "Outside country boundaries" (sea, offshore platforms, or islands missing from the boundary data).
method.regions: Indonesian provinces and Malaysian states: each detection takes the region of the nearest regency/district centre (data/fire-admin-lookup.json, from geoBoundaries). Approximate; detections near a boundary can land in the neighbouring region. Indonesian provinces follow the 2022 Papua split.
method.clusters: Connected 0.25° cells with detections (8-neighbour), complexes wider than 5 cells split around the strongest cells into pieces of at most 5 × 5 cells (about 1.25°); ranked by summed FRP. Period series cover the cluster cells plus their unclaimed neighbours. Names come from the nearest regency, district or province centre: approximate.
method.frp: Summed FRP adds every confident detection from every sensor and overpass, so one fire seen by four sensors counts four times. It is an index of fire activity, not an instantaneous total or emissions.
method.reference: Periods count back from the reference time: the latest moment every current sensor has delivered (one minute after the oldest "latest detection" among the four files), not the retrieval time, so the last 24 h are not short of a late pass. A sensor more than 36 h behind the freshest is listed in laggingSensors and does not hold the reference back.
method.history: Complete UTC days (ended by the reference time, after each file's first date), carried forward from earlier snapshots, at most 35 days.

grid.encoding: Per period, a flat list of 5 numbers per cell: [index delta, detections, summed FRP MW, max FRP MW, sensor mask]. Index = row * nCols + col on the frame with cellDeg; row = floor((lat - originLat) / cellDeg), col = floor((lon - originLon) / cellDeg). The first delta is the absolute index. Sensor mask bit i = sensors[i]. Cluster "cells" are absolute indices on the 0.25° frame.
